newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S. defense mergers turn up the heat in Europe.
newsitem.headline: U.S. defense mergers turn up the heat in Europe.

text.p: The planned $11.6 billion takeover of Northrop Grumman Corp. by Lockheed Martin Corp. is putting the heat on Europe to speed up its restructuring.
Europe is still fielding a large number of players in an increasingly competitive international market that will have to face both Lockheed Northrop and Boeing McDonnell Douglas.
Conscious of the threat, the industry is not sitting still. "Without structural changes, we will disappear," GEC Marconi chairman Geoffry Pattie said last month.

"Any move that strengthens the competitiveness of the U.S. defence industry is undermining the European defence industry and accelerates its decline," analyst Chris Avery at Paribas in London said on Friday.
"Boeing/McDonnell was a major move, Lockheed/Martin was a major move, this (Lockeed/Northrop) is another nail," Avery said.
The much-delayed restructuring of the French defence industry around Thomson-CSF and Aerospatiale could be a key factor behind a European realignment, analysts said.

The big names in the European defence industry, apart from Thomson, are British Aerospace Plc , General Electric Co Plc and Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG, and they are all engaged in an intricate multiple chess game to get the best from a European overhaul.
Shares in Thomson-CSF surged Friday, adding more than 4 percent to 169.80 francs at midday, in the wake of the Lockheed Northrop deal.

"This new operation in the defence sector will further increase the competitive pressures in the industry where Thomson-CSF is almost the single non-American supplier of significant size today," brokers Ferri said Friday.

Noting that Northrop was being acquired at 145 percent of its 1996 sales while Thomson-CSF's market value was 53 percent of its sales, the broker said this underlined "the undervaluation of the European leader in defence electronics."
But Avery said Thomson-CSF was not the linchpin of European defence and a restructuring was possible without it. He said that the French government's attitude was actually slowing down restructuring.
"The French government's attitude to cross-border asset transfers is an obtacle to an industry restructuring," he said.

The French state has a 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF and the previous centre-right government was weighing its options to sell to Lagardere Groupe -- associated with BAe -- or to Alcatel Alsthom , an ally of GEC.
The new Socialist-led government has said it will continue restructuring the defence industry around Thomson-CSF and Aerospatiale but has not yet made clear how it wants to proceed.

Industrialists are warning that time is running out. Even before the Lockheed/Northrop merger, and before the French change of government in early June, Alcatel chairman Serge Tchuruk said time was precious.
He said that if his bid with combat-plane maker Dassault Aviation for Thomson-CSF was successful he would immediately engage in alliance talks with European partners.
"It is a matter of weeks, not months," he said.
In Britain, rumours of a possible link between BAe and GEC were rekindled ahead of a key statement by chairman George Simpson next week.

GEC is on the point of concluding a global agreement with Finmeccanica of Italy. It is also a serious candidate to buy Siemens Defence, another major step in European consolidation due to its presence in large radar and communications programmes in Britain and Germany.
BAe recently took out an insurance policy against its not getting a key part in a European restructuring by teaming up with Lockheed Martin for the U.S. Joint Strike Fighter.
BAe is also a main contractor for the Eurofighter project with DASA, CASA of Spain and Alenia of Italy, which is still hanging on a thin thread due to German concerns about the project's costs.

BAe and DASA, with Aerospatiale of France and CASA, make up the Airbus civil plane consortium. While Airbus is slowly moving to become a single corporate entity, there is a growing consensus to include some military activities as well, such as a large transport plane.
